content.text: https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/pull/63
Out of scope for now:
Bag size limits (can use existing tools to split bags)
File naming conventions (specified outside the tool)
Enforcing metadata requirements (waiting on
Export appears to be working. However, when I try to validate it using the Ruby BagIt library, it's reporting bad checksums:

"expected /Users/awead/Projects/Fedora/fcrepo-import-export/hydra-export/data/rest/dev/32/ce/1a/60/32ce1a60-6676-4e4a-b8c2-406e616b4a00.ttl to have Digest::SHA1: 464189699A46660FD5FC2B5BF91002546C939CE6, actual is 464189699a46660fd5fc2b5bf91002546c939ce6"

However, this issue is that the export checksums are in upper case, but they're still correct. So I'm not sure if this is a problem with the ruby library or not. Any suggestions for a (better) validation process?

I've been editing the manifest-* files and replacing the single space with two spaces.  After that, I can validate them with shasum and mdsum.  There's a related ticket we filed in the bagit-java about the format of the manifest files not being compatible with the standard command-line tools:
https://github.com/LibraryOfCongress/bagit-java/issues/69
I see that
just closed that ticket, though, so I'll need to think about what the best validation strategy is.
: is the Ruby BagIt tool you are you using
https://github.com/tipr/bagit
?  I think we should file a bug if it can't handle uppercase letters in the checksums.
Yes, and yes.

My apologizes if I closed that ticket prematurely, their response seemed to orbit around only using BagIt tools to verify BagIt manifests. Which (while I don't necessarily agree with) I can see their point that these manifest files while
looking
like shasum manifests
aren't
I filled a ticket for the Ruby BagIt gem:
https://github.com/tipr/bagit/issues/27
I'll add that I installed the
Bagit-python
tool and was able to validate the bags very easily.

BTW, I noticed that the uppercase letters are the result of the hex-encoding method we were using.  I just pushed a new commit to that PR that switches to using Commons Codec's Hex.encodeHex, which produces lowercase letters (and is supposed to be faster, too).  Both of them are in the dependency tree already anyway.

: Don't worry about closing that ticket.  It seems less and less likely that they'll be open to a change, so I don't think it's necessarily worth your time to try to press them.  Being compatible with commonly-available tools is a big pet peeve of mine, so I'll keep at it a big longer.
I was just adding an IT for some changes related to importing bags and I think I should have written a better IT for export too. I am getting this related message on my new test.

java.lang.RuntimeException: Error verifying bag: File [/sw/var/www/fcrepo4/fcrepo-import-export/target/test-classes/sample/bag/data/fcrepo/rest/1f2a607f-10ff-4e51-879c-ca9e58a9a3f2.ttl] is suppose to have a SHA-1 hash of [FED45878477099DB65DB909CFD14BF75646845F9] but was computed [fed45878477099db65db909cfd14bf75646845f9]
	at org.fcrepo.importexport.importer.Importer.verifyBag(Importer.java:480)
	at org.fcrepo.importexport.importer.Importer.<init>(Importer.java:126)
	at org.fcrepo.importexport.integration.BagItIT.testImportBag(BagItIT.java:115)
Caused by: gov.loc.repository.bagit.exceptions.CorruptChecksumException: File [/sw/var/www/fcrepo4/fcrepo-import-export/target/test-classes/sample/bag/data/fcrepo/rest/1f2a607f-10ff-4e51-879c-ca9e58a9a3f2.ttl] is suppose to have a SHA-1 hash of [FED45878477099DB65DB909CFD14BF75646845F9] but was computed [fed45878477099db65db909cfd14bf75646845f9]
My latest commit (
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/pull/63/commits/067d7d25459855cb922b83d23391db2ef0188704)
generates lowercase checksums.  But maybe the test should use
equalsIgnoreCase
I agree, but I'm not going back to LoC to suggest that. Your latest commit should fix it.
Thanks,

, I can now validate with the Ruby gem. I've exported the hydra dataset with each profile: default, metaarchive, and aptrust. Each works correctly and is valid. However, I'm not seeing any differences between the profiles. Is that out of scope for this ticket?
There's no support for user-supplied metadata yet, so that's the big change in profiles that isn't implemented.
But there should be SHA-1 and SHA-256 manifests when you use the APTrust profile, and just SHA-1 when using the default or MetaArchive profiles.
yep, confirmed. OK, this is good to go.
Resolved with
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-import-export/commit/aa8f25c18a9754a64eb9659b93a9103800e3ffe3
Add support for parsing BagIt profiles.  At a minimum, use the profile to determine:
1. Which digest algorithm(s) to use
2. If the required metadata fields have been supplied
